title: First Year Engagement and Success Milestones: Manager & People Ops Playbook
author: Jordan Patel
content:
Overview:

This playbook standardizes the first-year engagement lifecycle for new hires at Redwood Inference. It provides managers and People Ops a shared set of milestones, checklists, measurement targets, and intervention patterns designed to maximize time-to-impact and reduce early attrition.

Audience:
- Hiring managers
- People Ops partners and onboarding coordinators
- Mentors and hiring teams

Goals and success metrics (KLIs/OKRs):
- Time-to-productivity: target 90% of core role ramp tasks completed by 90 days.
- 6-month retention target: >= 92%.
- 12-month retention target: >= 88%.
- Onboarding completion rate (checklist & trainings): >= 95% at 30 days.
- Manager 1:1 cadence adherence: >= 90% scheduled and held in first 12 weeks.

Quick reference: Responsibilities
- Hiring manager: role onboarding plan, first 30/60/90 review, performance calibration input, weekly 1:1s.
- Buddy/Mentor: day-to-day questions, team norms, shadowing.
- People Ops: admin and benefits setup, org orientation sessions, periodic check-ins (30/90/180/360), escalation support.

Milestone calendar (high-level):
1) Pre-boarding (Offer -> Day 0)
   - HR: send welcome kit, access instructions, hardware timeline, prework links.
   - Manager: role context email + 30/60/90 draft, invite to team Slack channel, calendar 1:1 for Day 1.
   - Target: All accounts provisioned 48 hours before start.

2) Day 1–7 (Orientation & immediate enablement)
   - Activities: org orientation (People Ops), team intro, set up dev environment / access, buddy assigned, first-week goals.
   - Deliverable: Completed "New Hire Access & Checklist" and at least one low-risk task merged (if role requires).

3) Week 2–4 (Foundational learning)
   - Activities: product orientation, core codebase walkthrough, internal docs scavenger hunt, security/compliance training (if applicable).
   - Manager touchpoints: weekly 1:1, first 30-day check-in meeting to review progress and blockers.
   - Deliverable: 30-day self-reflection + manager assessment filled in People Ops template.

4) 30–90 days (Ramp & contribution)
   - Activities: ownership of a small project, cross-functional introductions, begin regular roadmap meetings.
   - Deliverable: 30/60/90 goals updated; manager-led 60-day review; demonstrable contribution to a product or infra change.

5) 3–6 months (Broader impact)
   - Activities: lead a medium-scope initiative, present a learnings session for team, participate in calibration cycle.
   - Deliverable: 6-month review with evidence of impact, updated career development plan.

6) 6–12 months (Stabilize & grow)
   - Activities: take on steady ownership, mentor newer hires, propose improvement projects.
   - Deliverable: 12-month performance review, promotion/readiness signals if applicable.

Manager playbook: 30/60/90 and first-year checklists
- Before start: confirm access, onboarding calendar, assign buddy, prepare first-week tasks.
- Days 1–7: run orientation, set expectations for communication and meetings, walk through success criteria for 90 days.
- Weeks 2–4: verify training completions, unblock access issues, ensure the hire has at least one small deliverable.
- 30-day review (structured):
  1) Employee self-assessment (skills learned, blockers, what excites them).
  2) Manager assessment (progress vs. 30-day goals, behavioral fit, immediate needs).
  3) Clear list of items for 60 days and owners.
- 60-day review: check technical ownership, cross-team relationships, and readiness for a medium-scope project.
- 90-day review: confirm ramp targets met, adjust role expectations or support where needed.
- 6-month & 12-month reviews: document achievements, development areas, and career roadmap recommendations.

Sample 30/60/90 template (copyable):
- Role: [Role title]
- 30-day objectives: [Learning goals, access, first deliverable]
- 60-day objectives: [Ownership, small project deliverable, cross-team syncs]
- 90-day objectives: [Sustained throughput, independent delivery, knowledge sharing]
- Success metrics: [List measurable outcomes]

Feedback and performance cycle integration
- All first-year reviews feed into the standard Redwood performance cycle (quarterly calibration).
- For probationary or new-hire-specific reviews, use the "New Hire Review" tag during calibration so People Ops can apply reconciliation policies (probation extensions, targeted coaching plans).
- Suggested feedback cadence: weekly 1:1s for first 12 weeks, biweekly for months 4–6, monthly check-ins thereafter unless otherwise agreed.

Early-warning signals & interventions
- Missed milestones: two consecutive missed sprint commitments or training modules not completed by 45 days -> trigger a diagnostic check (owner: manager + People Ops).
- Engagement dip: negative sentiment in 1:1s, declining participation in team rituals, missed social integration -> schedule skip-level check-in and re-align onboarding tasks.
- Productivity gap: < 60% completion of role ramp checklist by 60 days -> create a Performance Improvement Path (PIP-lite) with explicit support and 30-day checkpoints.

Intervention patterns (templates and steps)
1) Diagnostic session (2 hours): manager + People Ops + employee. Output: action plan with owners and dates.
2) Focused mentoring: assign senior mentor, schedule weekly pairing.
3) Access & tooling remediation: escalate to eng-devex within 24 hours for infra blockers.
4) Escalation to manager of manager: if no measurable improvement after 30 days of remediation, involve DTL for role-level re-evaluation.

Retention & engagement initiatives specific to first year
- Peer cohort meetups: monthly cross-hire cohort sessions for knowledge sharing and community building.
- Buddy handoff: after month 3, transition from daily buddy to periodic mentor check-ins.
- Early-career development stipend: $1,200 discretionary learning budget available in first year for conferences/courses (requires manager pre-approval).

Integration with People Ops systems and templates
- Required forms: New Hire Checklist (HR001), 30-day Review (HR002), 6-month Review (HR006). Stored in People Ops Confluence templates.
- Tools: HRIS entry (Workday), onboarding tracker (Notion/Sheets), learning content (LMS), internal OKR tracker.
- Automation: People Ops will trigger calendar invites and reminders for 30/90/180/360 check-ins via the onboarding tracker.

Measurements and dashboards to monitor success
- Dashboard KPIs to monitor weekly: provisioned accounts % (target 98%), first-week task completion %, 30-day review submission rate, 6-month retention.
- People Ops owner: running monthly cohort analysis and flagging teams with >2 hires below ramp targets.

Manager FAQ
Q: What if the hire needs more technical ramp time?
A: Use the 60–90-day extension plan: adjust objectives, add shadowing and pair-programming and document progress weekly. Notify People Ops if an extension is planned beyond the standard probation period.

Q: When should I start promotion conversations?
A: Promotion readiness is typically assessed at the 12-month mark after evidence of consistent impact across multiple quarters and calibration input. Early conversations about growth expectations should begin at month 6.

Q: How do we handle international hires with different notice/start policies?
A: Coordinate with People Ops early in offer stage. Ensure local labor law adherence, localized benefits briefings, and adjust the pre-boarding timeline where needed.

Appendices
- Appendix A: Example 30-day self-reflection questions (copyable)
  1) What did I learn this month? 2) What were the biggest blockers? 3) What would help me be more effective?
- Appendix B: Standard timeline checklist (bullet list of admin items: payroll, benefits enrollment, security training, repo access, pager rotation opt-in).
- Appendix C: Sample messaging for skip-level check-in (email template)
  Subject: Quick skip-level sync to check on your onboarding experience
  Body: Hi [Name], I wanted to check in on how your first few months have felt. Please share any blockers, wins, or suggestions — happy to block 30 minutes this week.

Ownership and governance
- People Ops owns the playbook and quarterly updates.
- Managers own execution for their direct reports and provide calibration input.
- Engineering leadership: provide resources for dedicated ramp projects in the first 90 days.
